docs.title: Pattrie
docs.text:
Fast IP prefix trie for Python with a Rust backend. Supports longest-prefix match (LPM) lookups on IPv4 and IPv6 networks.

Built with PyO3 and the prefix-trie crate.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install pattrie

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
import pattrie

t = pattrie.Pattrie()
t["10.0.0.0/8"] = "rfc1918"
t["10.1.0.0/16"] = "internal"

t["10.1.2.3"]          # "internal"  (longest-prefix match)
t["10.2.0.1"]          # "rfc1918"
"10.1.2.3" in t        # True
t.get_key("10.1.2.3")  # "10.1.0.0/16"
t.get("192.0.2.1")     # None

Keys can be strings, ipaddress.IPv4Address, IPv4Network, IPv6Address, or IPv6Network. Keys may also be raw address bytes — a bytes/bytearray/memoryview of length 4 (IPv4) or 16 (IPv6), or a (bytes, prefixlen) tuple — useful for packet processing where the address is already in bytes.

docs.title: IPv6
docs.text:
import socket
import pattrie

t = pattrie.Pattrie(128, socket.AF_INET6)
t["2001:db8::/32"] = "documentation"
t["fe80::/10"] = "link-local"

t["fe80::1"]  # "link-local"

docs.title: Concurrent Reads with freeze()
docs.text:
After freeze(), read operations release the GIL, allowing true parallel lookups from multiple threads:

t = pattrie.Pattrie()
# ... populate ...
t.freeze()  # trie becomes read-only; reads release the GIL

# Safe to call from many threads simultaneously
value = t["10.1.2.3"]

t.thaw()    # restore mutability

docs.title: Cross-Process Sharing with dump() / load()
docs.text:
Serialize a frozen trie to a binary file and load it back in another process:

# Writer process
t = pattrie.Pattrie()
t["10.0.0.0/8"] = "rfc1918"
t.freeze()
t.dump("routes.ptri")

# Reader process
t2 = pattrie.Pattrie.load("routes.ptri")
t2["10.1.2.3"]  # "rfc1918"

docs.title: pattrie.Pattrie
docs.text:
A longest-prefix-match (LPM) IP prefix trie.

Stores arbitrary Python values keyed by IP prefixes. Lookups return the value associated with the longest matching prefix.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default maxbits

Maximum prefix length accepted (1–32 for IPv4, 1–128 for IPv6). Defaults to 32.

required family

Address family — socket.AF_INET (default) or socket.AF_INET6.

required

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If family is not AF_INET or AF_INET6, or if maxbits is out of range for the chosen family.

Example 
import pattrie

t = pattrie.Pattrie()
t["10.0.0.0/8"] = "rfc1918"
t["10.1.0.0/16"] = "internal"

t["10.1.2.3"]  # → "internal"  (longest match wins)
t["10.2.0.1"]  # → "rfc1918"

docs.title: insert_many(items: Iterable[tuple[NetworkKey, object]]) -> None
docs.text:
Insert multiple prefixes in one call.

Accepts any iterable of (prefix, value) pairs. All keys are parsed and validated before any insertion begins — if a malformed prefix is encountered, ValueError is raised and the trie is unchanged. Trie mutations run without the GIL for improved throughput on large loads.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default items Iterable[tuple[NetworkKey, object]]

An iterable of (prefix, value) pairs. Each prefix may be a CIDR string, IPv4Network, IPv6Network, or raw address bytes (bytes or a (bytes, prefixlen) tuple).

required

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the trie is frozen, a prefix is malformed, or a prefix length exceeds maxbits.

Example 
t = Pattrie()
t.insert_many([
    ("10.0.0.0/8", "rfc1918"),
    ("192.168.0.0/16", "home"),
])

docs.title: __setitem__(key: NetworkKey, value: object) -> None
docs.text:
Insert or replace a prefix using t[prefix] = value.

Equivalent to insert(prefix, value). Host bits are zeroed before insertion ("10.1.2.3/8" is stored as "10.0.0.0/8").

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the trie is frozen or the prefix is invalid.

docs.title: __getitem__(key: AddressKey) -> object
docs.text:
Longest-prefix-match lookup using t[key].

Returns the value stored for the longest matching prefix.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default key AddressKey

An IP address or network prefix (string, IPv4Address, IPv6Address, IPv4Network, IPv6Network, or raw address bytes — bytes/bytearray/memoryview or a (bytes, prefixlen) tuple).

required

Returns:

Type Description object

The value for the longest matching prefix.

Raises:

Type Description KeyError

If no prefix in the trie covers key.

docs.title: __delitem__(key: NetworkKey) -> None
docs.text:
Delete a prefix using del t[prefix].

Requires an exact match. Host bits are zeroed before lookup.

Raises:

Type Description KeyError

If the prefix is not in the trie.

ValueError

If the trie is frozen or the prefix is invalid.

docs.title: __contains__(key: AddressKey) -> bool
docs.text:
Return True if any prefix in the trie covers key (LPM semantics).

Does not raise on invalid or unrecognised keys — returns False instead.

docs.title: __len__() -> int
docs.text: Return the number of prefixes stored in the trie.

docs.title: __iter__() -> Iterator[str]
docs.text: Iterate over all stored prefixes as CIDR strings.

docs.title: __hash__() -> int
docs.text: Always raises TypeError: Pattrie is mutable and unhashable.

docs.title: get(key: AddressKey, default: object = None) -> object
docs.text:
Longest-prefix-match lookup, returning default on a miss.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default key AddressKey

An IP address or network prefix.

required default object

Value to return when no prefix matches. Defaults to None.

None

Returns:

Type Description object

The matched value, or default.

docs.title: get_many(keys: Sequence[AddressKey], default: object = None) -> list[object]
docs.text:
Look up multiple keys in one call, returning a list of values.

Each key is resolved by longest-prefix match; misses return default. When the trie is frozen, all trie traversals run without the GIL, enabling true parallel use from multiple threads. All key forms (strings, ipaddress objects, raw bytes, and (bytes, prefixlen) tuples) are supported in both frozen and non-frozen modes.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default keys Sequence[AddressKey]

A sequence of IP addresses or network prefixes.

required default object

Value to return for each miss. Defaults to None.

None

Returns:

Type Description list[object]

A list of matched values (or default) in the same order as

list[object]

keys.

docs.title: get_key(key: AddressKey, bare: bool = False) -> str | None
docs.text:
Return the matching prefix for a longest-prefix-match lookup.

Unlike __getitem__, returns the prefix string (e.g. "10.0.0.0/8") rather than the stored value.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default key AddressKey

An IP address or network prefix.

required bare bool

When True, strip the /len suffix and return only the network address. Defaults to False (full CIDR form).

False

Returns:

Type Description str | None

The matched prefix string, or None on a miss.

Note

Bare output is lossy — the prefix length is discarded and the result cannot be round-tripped back into the same prefix. Use this flag for display or interop, not for re-insertion.

docs.title: has_key(key: NetworkKey) -> bool
docs.text:
Return True if key is an exact prefix in the trie.

Unlike __contains__, this requires an exact match — no longest-prefix semantics.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default key NetworkKey

A network prefix (string, IPv4Network, IPv6Network, or raw address bytes — bytes or a (bytes, prefixlen) tuple).

required

Returns:

Type Description bool

True if the exact prefix exists, False otherwise.

docs.title: delete(key: NetworkKey) -> None
docs.text:
Delete an exact prefix from the trie.

Equivalent to del t[prefix]. Host bits are zeroed before lookup.

Raises:

Type Description KeyError

If the prefix is not in the trie.

ValueError

If the trie is frozen or the prefix is invalid.

docs.title: clear() -> None
docs.text:
Remove all entries from the trie.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the trie is frozen.

docs.title: setdefault(key: NetworkKey, default: object = None) -> object
docs.text:
Insert key with default if absent; return the current value.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default key NetworkKey

A network prefix (host bits are zeroed).

required default object

Value to insert when key is absent. Defaults to None.

None

Returns:

Type Description object

The existing value if key is present, otherwise default.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the trie is frozen and key is not present, or the prefix is invalid.

docs.title: update(other: Mapping[NetworkKey, object] | Iterable[tuple[NetworkKey, object]] | Pattrie) -> None
docs.text:
Merge entries from a mapping or iterable of pairs.

Accepts a dict, another Pattrie, or any iterable of (prefix, value) pairs. Existing keys are overwritten.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default other Mapping[NetworkKey, object] | Iterable[tuple[NetworkKey, object]] | Pattrie

A mapping with an .items() method or an iterable of (prefix, value) pairs.

required

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the trie is frozen, a prefix is malformed, or a prefix length exceeds maxbits.

docs.title: keys(bare: bool = False) -> list[str]
docs.text:
Return a list of all stored prefixes.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default bare bool

When True, strip the /len suffix and return only the network address (e.g. "10.1.0.0" instead of "10.1.0.0/24"). Defaults to False (full CIDR form).

False Note

Bare output is lossy — the prefix length is discarded and the result cannot be round-tripped back into the same prefix. Use this flag for display or interop, not for re-insertion. Two distinct prefixes with the same network address but different lengths (e.g. "10.0.0.0/8" and "10.0.0.0/16") produce duplicate bare keys — building a dict from bare output will silently drop all but one entry for each collision.

docs.title: values() -> list[object]
docs.text:
Return a list of all stored values in trie traversal order.

Order matches keys() — the i-th value corresponds to the i-th key.

docs.title: items(bare: bool = False) -> list[tuple[str, object]]
docs.text:
Return a list of (prefix, value) pairs in trie traversal order.

Each element is a two-tuple of the prefix string and its associated value, in the same order as keys().

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default bare bool

When True, strip the /len suffix from each key, returning only the network address. Defaults to False (full CIDR form).

False Note

Bare output is lossy — the prefix length is discarded and the result cannot be round-tripped back into the same prefix. Use this flag for display or interop, not for re-insertion. Two distinct prefixes with the same network address but different lengths (e.g. "10.0.0.0/8" and "10.0.0.0/16") produce duplicate bare keys — dict(t.items(bare=True)) will silently drop all but one entry for each collision.

docs.title: children(prefix: NetworkKey, bare: bool = False) -> list[str]
docs.text:
Return all prefixes in the trie more specific than prefix.

Uses longest-prefix containment: any stored prefix whose address range is entirely within prefix is included at any depth. The queried prefix itself is never included in the result. Returns [] when no descendants exist or the trie is empty.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default prefix NetworkKey

The parent prefix to query (CIDR string, IPv4Network, IPv6Network, or raw address bytes — bytes or a (bytes, prefixlen) tuple). Host bits are zeroed before lookup.

required bare bool

When True, strip the /len suffix from each result, returning only the network address. Defaults to False (full CIDR form).

False

Returns:

Type Description list[str]

A list of prefix strings for all stored prefixes contained within

list[str]

prefix. Order is lexicographic (prefix-trie traversal order).

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If prefix belongs to the wrong address family or is malformed.

Example 
t = Pattrie()
t["10.0.0.0/8"] = "a"
t["10.1.0.0/16"] = "b"
t["10.1.1.0/24"] = "c"
t["10.2.0.0/16"] = "d"

t.children("10.0.0.0/8")
# → ["10.1.0.0/16", "10.1.1.0/24", "10.2.0.0/16"]

t.children("10.0.0.0/9")   # not stored — still returns descendants
# → ["10.1.0.0/16", "10.1.1.0/24"]

docs.title: get_all(key: AddressKey) -> list[tuple[str, object]]
docs.text:
Return all covering prefixes for key, most-specific first.

Walks the full longest-prefix-match chain and returns every stored prefix that covers key, ordered from most specific (longest prefix length) to least specific (shortest prefix length). Returns an empty list when no prefix in the trie covers key.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default key AddressKey

An IP address or network prefix (string, IPv4Address, IPv6Address, IPv4Network, IPv6Network, raw address bytes — bytes/bytearray/memoryview or a (bytes, prefixlen) tuple).

required

Returns:

Type Description list[tuple[str, object]]

A list of (prefix, value) tuples in most-specific-first

list[tuple[str, object]]

order.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If key belongs to the wrong address family or is malformed.

Example 
t = Pattrie()
t["0.0.0.0/0"] = "default"
t["10.0.0.0/8"] = "rfc1918"
t["10.1.0.0/16"] = "internal"

t.get_all("10.1.2.3")
# → [("10.1.0.0/16", "internal"), ("10.0.0.0/8", "rfc1918"), ("0.0.0.0/0", "default")]

t.get_all("192.168.0.1")
# → [("0.0.0.0/0", "default")]

t.get_all("1.2.3.4")   # no covering prefix
# → []

docs.title: parent(prefix: NetworkKey, bare: bool = False) -> str | None
docs.text:
Return the closest covering prefix for prefix.

Returns the longest stored prefix that contains prefix but is not prefix itself — i.e. the immediate ancestor in the stored prefix hierarchy. Returns None if no covering prefix exists.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default prefix NetworkKey

The prefix to query (CIDR string, IPv4Network, IPv6Network, or raw address bytes — bytes or a (bytes, prefixlen) tuple). Host bits are zeroed before lookup.

required bare bool

When True, strip the /len suffix from the result, returning only the network address. Defaults to False (full CIDR form).

False

Returns:

Type Description str | None

The prefix string of the longest stored prefix that covers

str | None

prefix, or None if no such prefix exists.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If prefix belongs to the wrong address family or is malformed.

Example 
t = Pattrie()
t["10.0.0.0/8"] = "a"
t["10.1.0.0/16"] = "b"
t["10.1.1.0/24"] = "c"

t.parent("10.1.1.0/24")   # → "10.1.0.0/16"
t.parent("10.1.0.0/16")   # → "10.0.0.0/8"
t.parent("10.0.0.0/8")    # → None

t.parent("10.2.0.0/16")   # → "10.0.0.0/8"  (not stored — still works)

docs.title: dump(path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> None
docs.text:
Serialize this frozen trie to a binary file.

The file can be loaded in another process with Pattrie.load(). The trie must be frozen before calling this method.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str | PathLike[str]

Destination file path.

required

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the trie is not frozen or the file cannot be created.

docs.title: load(path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> Pattrie classmethod
docs.text:
Load a trie from a binary file written by dump().

Uses memory-mapped I/O for efficiency. The returned trie is frozen.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str | PathLike[str]

Path to a file written by dump().

required

Returns:

Type Description Pattrie

A new frozen Pattrie instance.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the file is not a valid pattrie dump or is corrupt.

docs.title: add(key: NetworkKey) -> None
docs.text:
Insert a prefix without a value (set-style).

Stores None as the sentinel value for the prefix. If the prefix is already present with an existing value, that value is left intact — add never destroys data.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default key NetworkKey

A network prefix (CIDR string, IPv4Network, IPv6Network, or raw address bytes). Host bits are zeroed before insertion.

required

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the trie is frozen, the prefix is malformed, or the prefix length exceeds maxbits.

docs.title: discard(key: NetworkKey) -> None
docs.text:
Remove a prefix if present; no-op if absent.

Unlike delete/__delitem__, does not raise KeyError when the prefix is not found.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default key NetworkKey

A network prefix (CIDR string, IPv4Network, IPv6Network, or raw address bytes). Host bits are zeroed before lookup.

required

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the trie is frozen or the prefix is malformed.

docs.title: freeze() -> None
docs.text:
Make the trie read-only and enable GIL-free concurrent reads.

After freezing, __getitem__, get, get_many, and __contains__ all release the GIL, allowing true parallel lookups from multiple threads. Any mutation attempt raises ValueError.

Use thaw() to restore mutability.

docs.title: thaw() -> None
docs.text:
Restore mutability after freeze().

Read operations will re-acquire the GIL. Mutations are allowed again.
